tooltip: AWB Presets – Locks the auto white balance or selects a white balance preset
content1:
Controls the auto white balance (AWB) behaviour of the camera.
  1. AWB Lock – Enables or disables the AWB lock. When enabled, the white balance value is locked to the current value. This prevents the camera from continuously adjusting the white balance in response to changing lighting conditions.
  2. AWB Preset – Sets the white balance preset mode. The camera provides several preset modes optimized for different lighting conditions, ranging from outdoor daylight to indoor tungsten lighting: Cloudy, DayLight, Flash, Cool White Fluorescent, Tungsten, CandleLight, Horizon, Custom and Auto.
content2:
AWBLockStatus160 Enum specifies the AWB lock state:
  1. LOCK_OFF (0x00) – AWB lock is disabled; the camera automatically adjusts white balance.
  2. LOCK_ON (0x01) – AWB lock is enabled; the white balance value is locked.

AWBPresetMode160 Enum specifies the white balance preset:
  1. CLOUDY (0x01) – Optimized for cloudy outdoor conditions.
  2. DAYLIGHT (0x02) – Optimized for daylight outdoor conditions.
  3. FLASH (0x03) – Optimized for flash illumination.
  4. COOLWHITE_FLUORESCENT (0x04) – Optimized for cool white fluorescent lights.
  5. TUNGSTEN (0x05) – Optimized for tungsten incandescent lights.
  6. CANDLELIGHT (0x06) – Optimized for candlelight.
  7. HORIZON (0x07) – Optimized for horizon lighting.
  8. CUSTOM (0x08) – Custom white balance value.
  9. AUTO (0x09) – Automatic white balance.

HID commands (sent with CAMERA_CONTROL_160, 0xAD): GET_AWB_LOCKSTATUS_160 (0x05) / SET_AWB_LOCKSTATUS_160 (0x06), GET_AWB_MODE_160 (0x03) / SET_AWB_MODE_160 (0x04).
getAPIDes: getAWBLockStatus retrieves the current AWB lock status and getAWBPresetMode retrieves the current AWB preset mode from the camera.
setAPIHeading:
bool setAWBLockStatus(AWBLockStatus160 lock)
bool setAWBPresetMode(AWBPresetMode160 awbMode)
setAPIDes: setAWBLockStatus sets the AWB lock status and setAWBPresetMode sets the AWB preset mode of the camera.

tooltip: Focus Mode Controls – Configures auto-focus status, lens position, AF lock, CAF scan range and auto-focus mode
content1:
Groups all focus related controls of the camera.
  1. Off – Enables or disables the auto-focus functionality. When checked, auto-focus is disabled and manual focus control is used; the auto-focus dependent controls are disabled. When unchecked, the camera automatically adjusts focus to keep the subject in focus.
  2. Manual focus Lens Position – Sets the manual focus lens position. Different positions are optimized for various focusing scenarios ranging from macro to infinity focus: INF position, Normal Position, Bar code position, Macro position, Initial DAC position and Custom Position.
  3. AF Lock – Locks the current auto-focus position. When enabled, the focus lens maintains its current position and does not adjust focus even if the scene or subject changes.
  4. CAF Scan Range – Configures the continuous auto-focus (CAF) scan range, i.e. the range of distances over which the camera searches for focus: Macro, Normal, Full, Infinity or Hyperfocal range mode.
  5. Auto Focus Modes – Continuous: the camera continuously adjusts focus to keep the subject in focus, even as the scene or subject changes. One-shot: the camera focuses once when triggered and then holds the focus position until explicitly refocused.
content2:
AFStatus160 Enum specifies the auto-focus status:
  1. AF_ON (0x00) – Auto-focus is enabled.
  2. AF_OFF (0x06) – Auto-focus is disabled (manual focus).

LensPosition160 Enum specifies the manual lens position:
  1. LENS_INFINITY (0x01) – Infinity focus (distant objects).
  2. NORMAL (0x02) – Normal focus distance.
  3. BARCODE (0x03) – Barcode scanning (shorter distance).
  4. LENS_MACRO (0x04) – Macro focus (very close objects).
  5. INITIAL_DAC (0x05) – Initial DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter) position.
  6. CUSTOM (0x06) – Custom user-defined position.

AFLockStatus160 Enum specifies the AF lock state:
  1. LOCK_OFF (0x00) – AF lock is disabled; auto-focus continues to adjust.
  2. LOCK_ON (0x01) – AF lock is enabled; the focal position is locked.

CAFScanRange160 Enum specifies the CAF scan range:
  1. MACRO (0x00) – Optimized for close-range/macro focusing.
  2. NORMAL (0x01) – Optimized for normal focusing distances.
  3. FULL (0x02) – Searches across the entire focus range.
  4. FOCUS_INFINITY (0x03) – Optimized for distant/infinity focusing.
  5. HYPERFOCAL (0x04) – Uses hyperfocal distance for maximum depth of field.

AFMode160 Enum specifies the auto-focus mode:
  1. ONESHOT (0x01) – Camera focuses once when triggered.
  2. CONTINUOUS (0x06) – Camera continuously adjusts focus (CAF mode).

HID commands (sent with CAMERA_CONTROL_160, 0xAD): GET_AF_STATUS_160 (0x15) / SET_AF_STATUS_160 (0x16), GET_LENS_POSITION_160 (0x13) / SET_LENS_POSITION_160 (0x14), GET_AF_LOCKSTATUS_160 (0x11) / SET_AF_LOCKSTATUS_160 (0x12), GET_CAF_RANGE_160 (0x0F) / SET_CAF_RANGE_160 (0x10), GET_AF_MODE_160 (0x01) / SET_AF_MODE_160 (0x02).
getAPIHeading:
bool getAFStatus(uint8_t &outStatus)
bool getManualLensPosition(uint8_t &outPosition)
bool getAFLockStatus(uint8_t &outLock)
bool getCAFScanRange(uint8_t &outRange)
bool getAFMode(uint8_t &outAfMode)
getAPIDes: These functions retrieve the current auto-focus status, manual lens position, AF lock status, CAF scan range and auto-focus mode from the camera.
setAPIHeading:
bool setAFStatus(AFStatus160 status)
bool setManualLensPosition(LensPosition160 position)
bool setAFLockStatus(AFLockStatus160 lock)
bool setCAFScanRange(CAFScanRange160 range)
bool setAFMode(AFMode160 afMode)
setAPIDes: These functions set the auto-focus status, manual lens position, AF lock status, CAF scan range and auto-focus mode of the camera.

tooltip: Q-Factor – Controls the JPEG compression quality factor of the camera
content1: Controls the JPEG compression quality factor of the camera output. A higher value results in better image quality with larger file sizes. The value ranges from 10 to 96.
content2:
1. getQFactor retrieves the current Q-Factor value.
2. setQFactor sets the Q-Factor value (range: 10–96).
getAPIDes: This function retrieves the current JPEG Q-Factor value from the camera.
setAPIDes: This function sets the JPEG Q-Factor of the camera (range: 10–96).

tooltip: AE Metering Mode – Locks the auto-exposure or selects the auto-exposure metering method
content1:
Controls the auto-exposure (AE) behaviour of the camera.
  1. AE Lock – Enables or disables the AE lock. When enabled, the exposure value is locked to the current value. This prevents the camera from continuously adjusting exposure in response to changing lighting conditions.
  2. AE Metering Mode – Configures the metering method used by the camera to measure scene brightness. Different metering modes are optimized for different scene compositions: Manual, Center-Weighted average, All block integral, Spot1 (small area) and Spot2 (large area).
content2:
AELockStatus160 Enum specifies the AE lock state:
  1. LOCK_OFF (0x00) – AE lock is disabled; the camera automatically adjusts exposure.
  2. LOCK_ON (0x01) – AE lock is enabled; the exposure value is locked.

AEMeteringMode160 Enum specifies the metering method:
  1. AE_OFF (0x00) – AE metering is disabled ("Manual" in the UI, manual exposure control).
  2. CENTER_WEIGHTED_AVG (0x01) – Gives more weight to the center of the frame.
  3. ALL_BLOCK_INTEGRAL (0x02) – Averages exposure across the entire frame.
  4. SMALL_AREA (0x05) – Meters exposure from a small area (Spot1).
  5. LARGE_AREA (0x06) – Meters exposure from a larger area (Spot2).

HID commands (sent with CAMERA_CONTROL_160, 0xAD): GET_AE_LOCK_STATUS_160 (0x09) / SET_AE_LOCK_STATUS_160 (0x0A), GET_AE_METERING_MODE_160 (0x07) / SET_AE_METERING_MODE_160 (0x08).
getAPIDes: getAELockStatus retrieves the current AE lock status and getAEMeteringMode retrieves the current AE metering mode from the camera.
setAPIHeading:
bool setAELockStatus(AELockStatus160 lock)
bool setAEMeteringMode(AEMeteringMode160 mode)
setAPIDes: setAELockStatus sets the AE lock status and setAEMeteringMode sets the AE metering mode of the camera.

tooltip: Burst Length – Sets the number of images to capture in a single burst
content1: Sets the number of images the camera captures in a single burst. Values range from 1 to 5 images per burst, allowing rapid sequential image capture.
content2:
1. getBurstLength retrieves the current burst length setting.
2. setBurstLength sets the burst length (range: 1–5).
getAPIDes: This function retrieves the current burst length value from the camera.
setAPIDes: This function sets the burst length (number of images per capture burst) of the camera.

tooltip: Anti-Flicker Mode – Compensates for flicker caused by artificial lighting
content1:
Configures compensation for flicker caused by artificial lighting.
  1. Off – Disables anti-flicker compensation. No compensation is applied for flicker caused by artificial lighting.
  2. Auto – Enables automatic flicker detection and compensation. The camera automatically detects the power line frequency (50 Hz or 60 Hz) and applies appropriate compensation.
  3. Manual – Enables manual selection of the power line frequency for flicker compensation using the Frequency drop-down, which is enabled only in this mode.
  4. Frequency – Selects 50 Hz (regions with 50 Hz power lines, e.g. Europe, Asia, Australia) or 60 Hz (regions with 60 Hz power lines, e.g. North America, South America, Japan).
content2:
FlickerMode160 Enum specifies the anti-flicker mode:
  1. AUTO_DETECTION (0x00) – Automatically detects and compensates for flicker (Auto).
  2. FIFTY_HZ (0x01) – Compensates for 50 Hz power line frequency (Manual, 50 Hz).
  3. SIXTY_HZ (0x02) – Compensates for 60 Hz power line frequency (Manual, 60 Hz).
  4. FLICKER_OFF (0x04) – Anti-flicker compensation is disabled (Off).

HID commands (sent with CAMERA_CONTROL_160, 0xAD): GET_FLICKER_DETECTION_160 (0x0B) / SET_FLICKER_DETECTION_160 (0x0C).
getAPIDes: This function retrieves the current anti-flicker mode (and therefore the manual frequency) from the camera.
setAPIDes: This function sets the anti-flicker mode of the camera. Off, Auto and Manual (50 Hz / 60 Hz) all map to a single FlickerMode160 value.

tooltip: Firmware Version – Reads the firmware version string of the camera
content1: Reads the firmware version string from the main processor of the camera. This is a read-only property used to identify the firmware currently running on the device.
content2: 1. getFirmwareVersion retrieves the firmware version string. This is a read-only operation.
getAPIDes: This function retrieves the firmware version string from the camera.
setAPIDes: Firmware Version is a read-only property. There is no set function available for this control.
setAPICode:
// No set API available for Firmware Version.
// Use getFirmwareVersion() to read the current firmware version.

tooltip: ISP Firmware Version – Reads the ISP firmware version string of the camera
content1: Reads the firmware version string from the Image Signal Processor (ISP) chip of the camera. This is a read-only property used to identify the ISP firmware currently running on the device.
content2: 1. getFirmwareVersion (or ISP-specific variant) retrieves the ISP firmware version string. This is a read-only operation.
getAPIDes: This function retrieves the ISP firmware version string from the camera.
setAPIDes: ISP Firmware Version is a read-only property. There is no set function available for this control.
setAPICode:
// No set API available for ISP Firmware Version.
// Use getFirmwareVersion() or getISPFirmwareVersion() to read the ISP firmware version.

tooltip: Default – Restores all camera settings to their factory defaults
content1: Restores all See3CAM_160 settings to their factory default values. After the command succeeds the application reads back all camera controls so the UI reflects the default values.
content2:
1. restoreDefault restores all camera settings to their factory default values.

HID command (sent with CAMERA_CONTROL_160, 0xAD): SET_TO_DEFAULT_160 (0xFF).
getAPIDes: Set to Default is a write-only action. There is no get function for this operation.
getAPICode:
// No get API available for Set to Default.
// Use restoreDefault() to restore the factory default settings.
setAPIDes: This function restores all camera settings to their factory defaults.
